ko.title: [부동산 기초 101 #14] 내 부동산이 보내는 두 가지 세금 고지서 — 매년 하나, 단 한 번 하나

segments.src: > Owning real estate means paying tax while you hold it and tax when you sell it — and good management is largely the work of shrinking both without shrinking the asset.
segments.tr: > 부동산을 소유한다는 것은 보유하는 동안 세금을 내고 매각할 때 세금을 낸다는 뜻이며, 좋은 관리는 자산을 줄이지 않으면서 이 두 가지를 모두 줄이는 작업입니다.

segments.src: Most people think of a property as a thing you buy.
segments.tr: 대부분의 사람들은 부동산을 사는 물건으로 생각합니다.

segments.src: In practice it's a small business you run, and like any business it has an operating side and a tax side.
segments.tr: 실제로 그것은 운영하는 소규모 사업이며, 모든 사업과 마찬가지로 운영 측면과 세 금 측면이 있습니다.

segments.src: *Property management* is the day-to-day: finding tenants, collecting rent, fixing the water heater at 11 p.m., handling turnovers, keeping the building code-compliant.
segments.tr: *부동산 관리*는 일상적인 업무입니다: 세입자 찾기, 임대료 수령, 밤 11시에 온수기 수리, 교체 작업 처리, 건물 규정 준수 유지.

segments.src: In the U.S., a residential property manager typically charges **8–10% of collected rent**, often plus a leasing fee of half to one month's rent each time a unit turns over.
segments.tr: 미국에서는 주거용 부동산 관리자가 일반적으로 **수령한 임대료의 8–10%**를 청구하며, 유닛이 교체될 때마다 임대료의 반에서 한 달 치에 해당하는 임대 수수료를 추가로 받는 경우가 많습니다.

segments.src: *Asset management* is the level above it: Should we hold or sell?
segments.tr: *자산 관리*는 그 상위 단계입니다: 보유할 것인가 매각할 것인가?

segments.src: Spend $40,000 on a kitchen renovation to push rents, or spend nothing and harvest cash?
segments.tr: 임대료를 올리기 위해 주방 리모델링에 40,000달러를 쓸 것인가, 아니면 아무것도 쓰지 않고 현금을 회수할 것인가?

segments.src: Property management protects the income; asset management decides what the income is *for*.
segments.tr: 부동산 관리는 수입을 보호하고, 자산 관리는 그 수입이 *무엇을 위한* 것인지 결정합니다.

segments.src: Both are measured through one number: **Net Operating Income (NOI)**.
segments.tr: 두 가지 모두 하나의 숫자로 측정됩니다: **순영업소득 (NOI)**.

segments.src: NOI = effective gross income − operating expenses
segments.tr: NOI = effective gross income − operating expenses

segments.src: Operating expenses include property taxes, insurance, maintenance, management fees, and utilities you cover.
segments.tr: 운영 비용에는 재산세, 보험료, 유지보수비, 관리비, 그리고 본인이 부담하는 공과금이 포함됩니다.

segments.src: They **exclude** your mortgage payment and depreciation.
That's deliberate — NOI describes the property, not your financing.
segments.tr: 이는 의도된 것입니다 — NOI는 자금 조달 방식이 아니라 부동산 자체를 설명합니다.

segments.src: **The tax side: two very different bills.**
segments.tr: **세금 측면: 완전히 다른 두 가지 고지서.**

segments.src: **1) The annual bill — property tax (the "holding tax").** In the U.S.
this is levied locally, not federally: by counties, cities, and school districts.
segments.tr: 이는 연방 정부가 아니라 카운티, 도시, 학군 등 지역 단위로 부과됩니다.

segments.src: The county assessor sets an *assessed value*, and a tax rate (often quoted in *mills* — dollars per $1,000 of value) is applied to it.
segments.tr: 카운티 평가사는 *과세 표준 가치*를 설정하고, 여기에 세율(가치 1,000달러당 달러 단위인 *밀(mill)*로 자주 인용됨)이 적용됩니다.

segments.src: Effective rates vary enormously — roughly 0.3% of market value in Hawaii to well over 2% in New Jersey and parts of Illinois and Texas.
segments.tr: 실효 세율은 하와이의 시장 가치 약 0.3%에서 뉴저지 및 일리노이, 텍사스의 일부 지역의 2%를 훌쩍 넘는 수준까지 엄청나게 다양합니다.

segments.src: On the same $400,000 house, that's the difference between about $1,200 and $8,800 a year, every year, forever.
segments.tr: 동일한 400,000달러짜리 주택의 경우, 이는 매년, 영원히 매년 약 1,200달러와 8,800달러 사이의 차이입니다.

segments.src: Two things worth knowing: most states offer a **homestead exemption** that reduces the taxable value of your primary residence, and every state has a formal **assessment appeal** process.
segments.tr: 알아둘 가치가 있는 두 가지 사실: 대부분의 주는 거주 주택의 과세 표준 가치를 낮춰주는 **면세 혜택(homestead exemption)**을 제공하며, 모든 주에는 공식적인 **평가 이의신청** 절차가 있습니다.

segments.src: Some states also cap how fast assessed value can rise — California's Proposition 13 limits the increase to 2% per year until the property sells, at which point it's reassessed at market value.
segments.tr: 또한 일부 주는 과세 표준 가치가 상승하는 속도에 상한선을 둡니다 — 캘리포니아의 발의안 13호는 부동산이 매각될 때까지 연간 인상률을 2%로 제한하며, 매각 시점에 시장 가치로 재평가됩니다.

segments.src: **2) The one-time bill — capital gains tax (the "transfer tax").** When you sell, you're taxed on the *gain*, not the sale price:
segments.tr: **2) 일회성 고지서 — 자본 이득세 ("이전세").** 매각할 때, 판매 가격이 아니라 *차익*에 대해 과세됩니다:

segments.src: gain = amount realized (sale price − selling costs) − adjusted basis
segments.tr: gain = amount realized (sale price − selling costs) − adjusted basis

segments.src: adjusted basis = purchase price + capital improvements − depreciation taken
segments.tr: adjusted basis = purchase price + capital improvements − depreciation taken

segments.src: Hold longer than one year and the gain gets **long-term capital gains** rates (0%, 15%, or 20% federally, depending on income), plus a possible 3.8% Net Investment Income Tax at higher incomes, plus state tax.
segments.tr: 1년 이상 보유하면 차익에 대해 **장기 양도소득세** 세율(소득에 따라 연방 기준 0%, 15%, 20%)이 적용되며, 고소득의 경우 3.8%의 순투자소득세와 주 세금이 추가될 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Sell within a year and it's taxed as ordinary income — a materially worse outcome.
segments.tr: 1년 이내에 매각하면 일반 소득으로 과세되는데, 이는 훨씬 더 불리한 결과입니다.

segments.src: **The wrinkle that surprises everyone: depreciation recapture.** While you own a rental, the IRS lets you deduct the *building* (never the land) over **27.5 years** for residential property or **39 years** for commercial — a paper expense that shelters real cash income.
segments.tr: **모두를 놀라게 하는 함정: 감가상각 환수.** 임대 주택을 소유하는 동안 IRS는 주거용의 경우 **27.5년**, 상업용의 경우 **39년** 동안 토지가 아닌 *건물*을 공제할 수 있도록 허용합니다 — 이는 실제 현금 수입을 보호하는 서류상 비용입니다.

segments.src: But at sale, the depreciation you took gets pulled back into the gain as *unrecaptured Section 1250 gain*, taxed at up to 25%.
segments.tr: 그러나 매각 시, 받았던 감가상각비는 최대 25%의 세율이 적용되는 *환수되지 않은 섹션 1250 차익*으로 다시 차익에 합산됩니다.

segments.src: Depreciation is a deferral, not a gift.
And here's the trap: the IRS computes recapture on depreciation "allowed or allowable" — you owe it whether or not you actually claimed the deduction.
segments.tr: 그리고 여기에 함정이 있습니다. IRS는 "허용되거나 허용 가능한" 감가상각에 대해 환수를 계산합니다. 실제 공제를 청구했는지 여부와 상관없이 세금을 납부해야 합니다.

segments.src: Three legal off-ramps are worth knowing by name:
segments.tr: 이름을 알아둘 가가 있는 세 가지 합법적인 절세 방법:

segments.src: - **Section 121 exclusion** — sell your *primary residence* after living in it 2 of the last 5 years and exclude up to **$250,000** of gain (single) or **$500,000** (married filing jointly).
segments.tr: - **섹션 121 면제** — 지난 5년 중 2년 동안 거주한 후 *주거용 주택*을 매각하고 (단독) **250,000달러** 또는 (부부 공동 신고) **500,000달러**까지의 차익을 면제받습니다.

segments.src: - **Section 1031 like-kind exchange** — on *investment* property, roll the proceeds into another investment property and defer the gain. Strict clock: identify replacement property within **45 days**, close within **180 days**, and a qualified intermediary must hold the money. Since 2018 this applies to real property only.
segments.tr: - **섹션 1031 동종 교환** — *투자용* 부동산의 경우, 매각 대금을 다른 투자용 부동산에 재투자하여 차익을 유예합니다. 엄격한 일정: **45일** 이내에 대체 부동산을 지정하고 **180일** 이내에 거래를 완료해야 하며, 적격 중개인이 자금을 보유해야 합니다. 2018년 이후 이는 부동산에만 적용됩니다.

segments.src: - **Step-up in basis at death** — heirs generally inherit at fair market value, which can erase decades of embedded gain.
segments.tr: - **사망 시 취득가액 스텝업** — 상속인은 일반적으로 공정 시장 가치로 상속받으므로, 수십 년간 내재된 차익을 지울 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Say you buy a single-family rental in Columbus, Ohio for **$300,000**.
segments.tr: 오하이오주 콜럼버스의 단독 주택 임대 매물을 **300,000달러**에 구입했다고 가정해 보겠습니다.

segments.src: The county allocates $60,000 to land and $240,000 to the building.
You put $150,000 down and borrow $150,000 at 6.5%.
So your actual **cash flow is about $3,546**.
**Now the tax side of the same year:**
You put roughly $3,500 of cash in your pocket and report a **$3,500 loss**.
segments.tr: 주머니에 현금 약 3,500달러를 넣고 **3,500달러의 손실**을 신고합니다.

segments.src: That gap is depreciation doing its job.
segments.tr: 그 격차는 감가상각이 제 역할을 하고 있기 때문입니다.

segments.src: (Whether you can *use* that loss is a separate question — rental losses are generally "passive," though there's a special allowance of up to $25,000 for active participants, which phases out between $100,000 and $150,000 of modified AGI.)
segments.tr: (그 손실을 *사용*할 수 있는지는 별개의 문제입니다 — 임대 손실은 일반적으로 "수동적"이지만, 수정 AGI가 100,000달러에서 150,000달러 사이인 경우 단계적으로 폐지되는 적극적 참여자를 위한 최대 25,000달러의 특별 공제가 있습니다.)

segments.src: One nice detail: property taxes on a *rental* are an ordinary business expense on Schedule E and are **not** subject to the SALT cap that limits state and local tax deductions on your personal return.
segments.tr: 멋진 세부 사항 하나: *임대* 부동산의 재산세는 스케줄 E상의 일반적인 사업 비용이며, 개인 신고서의 주 및 지방세 공제를 제한하는 SALT 상한선의 적용을 **받지** 않습니다.

segments.src: The same dollar of property tax is treated very differently depending on whether you live in the house or rent it out.
segments.tr: 동일한 1달러의 재산세라도 집에 살고 있는지 아니면 임대하고 있는지에 따라 매우 다르게 취급됩니다.

segments.src: **Ten years later, you sell for $400,000** with 6% selling costs:
Notice: the property appreciated $100,000, but your taxable gain is $163,270.
segments.tr: 참고: 부동산 가치가 100,000달러 상승했지만, 과세 대상 차익은 163,270달러입니다.

segments.src: The extra $63,000-odd is the bill for ten years of depreciation deductions coming due — which is precisely why 1031 exchanges exist.
segments.tr: 추가로 발생한 63,000달러 가량은 10년 동안 누적된 감가상각 공제에 대한 청구서입니다 — 이것이 바로 1031 교환이 존재하는 이유입니다.

segments.src: 1. Property management protects NOI day to day; asset management decides when to hold, improve, refinance, or sell.
segments.tr: 1. 부동산 관리는 일상적인 NOI를 보호하고, 자산 관리는 보유, 개선, 재융자 또는 매각 시기를 결정합니다.

segments.src: 2. Property tax is local, annual, and permanent — effective rates range from under 0.5% to over 2% of value, so the *location* of a purchase is also a tax decision.
segments.tr: 2. 재산세는 지역적이고 연례적이며 영구적입니다 — 실효 세율은 가치의 0.5% 미만에서 2% 이상까지 다양하므로, 구매 *위치*도 세금 결정입니다.

segments.src: 3. Capital gains tax is computed on gain over adjusted basis, and depreciation lowers that basis — so the deduction you enjoy while holding is largely a deferral you settle at sale.
segments.tr: 3. 양도소득세는 조정 기준가액을 초과하는 차익에 대해 계산되며, 감가상각은 그 기준가액을 낮추므로 보유 기간 동안 누리는 공제는 대부분 매각 시 결산하는 유예입니다.

segments.src: **1.** Which of the following is **excluded** from operating expenses when calculating NOI?
segments.tr: **1.** NOI를 계산할 때 운영 비용에서 **제외**되는 것은 무엇입니까?

segments.src: a) Property taxes   b) Property management fees   c) Mortgage principal and interest   d) Landlord-paid insurance
segments.tr: a) 재산세   b) 부동산 관리 수수료   c) 모기지 원금 및 이자   d) 임대인이 지불하는 보험

segments.src: **2.** True or False: Residential rental buildings are depreciated over 27.5 years, and the land is depreciated over the same period.
segments.tr: **2.** 참 또는 거짓: 주거용 임대 건물은 27.5년에 걸쳐 감가상각되며, 토지도 같은 기간 동안 감가상각됩니다.

segments.src: **3.** You bought a rental for $300,000, made $20,000 of capital improvements, and took $50,000 of depreciation.
segments.tr: **3.** 300,000달러에 임대 주택을 매입하고, 20,000달러의 자본 개선을 수행했으며, 50,000달러의 감가상각을 받았습니다.

segments.src: - **NOI (Net Operating Income)** — Effective gross income minus operating expenses, before financing and depreciation; the standard measure of a property's earning power.
segments.tr: - **NOI (순영업소득)** — 자금 조달 및 감가상각 전, 유효 총소득에서 운영 비용을 뺀 금액; 부동산의 수익력을 나타내는 표준 측정치.

segments.src: - **Assessed value / mill rate** — The value a local assessor assigns to a property, and the tax rate applied to it, quoted as dollars per $1,000 of value.
segments.tr: - **과세 표준 가치 / 밀 세율** — 지역 평가사가 부동산에 부여하는 가치 및 이에 적용되는 세율로, 가치 1,000달러당 달러로 표시됩니다.

segments.src: - **Adjusted basis** — Purchase price plus capital improvements minus depreciation taken; the number your sale proceeds are measured against to compute gain.
segments.tr: - **조정 기준가액** — 구매 가격에 자본 개선 비용을 더하고 받은 감가상각을 뺀 금액; 차익을 계산하기 위해 매각 대금과 비교되는 수치.

segments.src: - **Depreciation recapture (unrecaptured §1250 gain)** — The portion of gain attributable to depreciation you previously deducted, taxed at up to 25% at sale.
segments.tr: - **감가상각 환수 (환수되지 않은 §1250 차익)** — 이전에 공제받은 감가상각에 기인하는 차익 부분으로, 매각 시 최대 25%의 세율이 부과됩니다.

segments.src: - **Section 1031 exchange** — A swap of one investment property for another that defers capital gains tax, subject to 45-day identification and 180-day closing deadlines.
segments.tr: - **섹션 1031 교환** — 45일 이내 지정 및 180일 이내 마감 기한에 따라 양도소득세를 유예하는 하나의 투자용 부동산을 다른 부동산으로 교환하는 것.

segments.src: *This is an educational overview of how U.S.
segments.tr: *이 내용은 미국 부동산 세금 제도의 구조에 대한 교육적 개요이며 세무 조언이 아닙니다.

segments.src: real estate taxation is structured, not tax advice.
segments.tr: 세율, 임계값, 상한선은 법에 따라 변경되며 주마다 다르므로 조치하기 전에 CPA와 현재 수치를 확인하십시오.*

segments.src: Rates, thresholds, and caps change with legislation and vary by state — confirm current figures with a CPA before acting.*

segments.tr: NOI는 자금 조달 방식과 독립적으로 부동산을 비교할 수 있도록 의도적으로 부채 서비스를 제외합니다.

segments.src: NOI deliberately excludes debt service so the property can be compared independently of how it was financed.

segments.tr: 27.5년 일정은 건물에만 적용되며 토지는 절대 감가상각되지 않으므로, 구매 가격을 둘 사이에 배분해야 합니다.

segments.src: The 27.5-year schedule applies to the building only; land is never depreciated, which is why the purchase price must be allocated between the two.

segments.tr: $300,000 + $20,000 − $50,000 = $270,000; 받는 감가상각의 모든 1달러는 기준가액을 낮추므로 결국 과세 대상 차익을 높이게 됩니다.*

segments.src: $300,000 + $20,000 − $50,000 = $270,000; every dollar of depreciation you take lowers your basis and therefore raises your eventual taxable gain.*
segments.tr: $300,000 + $20,000 − $50,000 = $270,000; 귀하가 받는 감가상각비 1달러마다 기준 가액이 낮아지고, 그 결과 향후 과세 대상 양도차익이 높아집니다.*

zh.title: [房地产 101 #14] 您的房产会向您发送两张税单——一张每年一次，一张仅一次

segments.src: > Owning real estate means paying tax while you hold it and tax when you sell it — and good management is largely the work of shrinking both without shrinking the asset.
segments.tr: > 拥有房地产意味着在持有期间需要纳税，在出售时也需要纳税——而良好的管理在很大程度上就是要在不缩减资产的前提下，尽可能减少这两项税负。

segments.src: Most people think of a property as a thing you buy.
segments.tr: 大多数人认为房产是你购买的一件物品。

segments.src: In practice it's a small business you run, and like any business it has an operating side and a tax side.
segments.tr: 实际上，它是一项你经营的小生意，像任何生意一样，它有运营层面和税务层面。

segments.src: *Property management* is the day-to-day: finding tenants, collecting rent, fixing the water heater at 11 p.m., handling turnovers, keeping the building code-compliant.
segments.tr: *物业管理*是日常事务：寻找租户、收取租金、在晚上11点修理热水器、处理租户更替、确保建筑符合规范。

segments.src: In the U.S., a residential property manager typically charges **8–10% of collected rent**, often plus a leasing fee of half to one month's rent each time a unit turns over.
segments.tr: 在美国，住宅物业经理通常收取**已收租金的 8–10%**，通常外加每次单位更替时半个月到一个月的租金作为租赁费。

segments.src: *Asset management* is the level above it: Should we hold or sell?
segments.tr: *资产管理*是更高一层的决策：我们应该持有还是出售？

segments.src: Spend $40,000 on a kitchen renovation to push rents, or spend nothing and harvest cash?
segments.tr: 花 40,000 美元进行厨房翻新以提高租金，还是什么都不做直接获取现金？

segments.src: Property management protects the income; asset management decides what the income is *for*.
segments.tr: 物业管理保护收入；资产管理决定收入的*用途*。

segments.src: Both are measured through one number: **Net Operating Income (NOI)**.
segments.tr: 两者都通过一个数字来衡量：**净营业收入 (NOI)**。

segments.src: NOI = effective gross income − operating expenses
segments.tr: NOI = effective gross income − operating expenses

segments.src: Operating expenses include property taxes, insurance, maintenance, management fees, and utilities you cover.
segments.tr: 运营费用包括房产税、保险、维护、管理费以及你承担的公用事业费用。

segments.src: They **exclude** your mortgage payment and depreciation.
segments.tr: 它们**不包括**你的抵押贷款还款和折旧。

segments.src: That's deliberate — NOI describes the property, not your financing.
segments.tr: 这是刻意为之的——NOI 描述的是房产本身，而不是你的融资情况。

segments.src: **The tax side: two very different bills.**
segments.tr: **税务层面：两笔截然不同的税款。**

segments.src: **1) The annual bill — property tax (the "holding tax").** In the U.S.
segments.tr: **1) 年度税单——房产税（“持有税”）。** 在美国，

segments.src: this is levied locally, not federally: by counties, cities, and school districts.
segments.tr: 这是由地方而非联邦征收的：由县、市和学区征收。

segments.src: The county assessor sets an *assessed value*, and a tax rate (often quoted in *mills* — dollars per $1,000 of value) is applied to it.
segments.tr: 县评估员设定一个*评估价值*，并对其应用税率（通常以*密尔 (mills)* 为单位报价——即每 1,000 美元价值对应的美元金额）。

segments.src: Effective rates vary enormously — roughly 0.3% of market value in Hawaii to well over 2% in New Jersey and parts of Illinois and Texas.
segments.tr: 有效税率差异巨大——从夏威夷的市场价值约 0.3% 到新泽西州以及伊利诺伊州和德克萨斯州部分地区的 2% 以上不等。

segments.src: On the same $400,000 house, that's the difference between about $1,200 and $8,800 a year, every year, forever.
segments.tr: 对于同一套 400,000 美元的房子，这意味着每年、永远每年，大约 1,200 美元和 8,800 美元之间的差异。

segments.src: Two things worth knowing: most states offer a **homestead exemption** that reduces the taxable value of your primary residence, and every state has a formal **assessment appeal** process.
segments.tr: 有两件事值得了解：大多数州提供**宅基地豁免 (homestead exemption)**，可以降低你主要住所的应纳税价值，而且每个州都有正式的**评估申诉 (assessment appeal)** 程序。

segments.src: Some states also cap how fast assessed value can rise — California's Proposition 13 limits the increase to 2% per year until the property sells, at which point it's reassessed at market value.
segments.tr: 一些州还限制了评估价值的上涨速度——加州的第 13 号提案将每年的增长限制在 2%，直到房产出售，届时将按市场价值重新评估。

segments.src: **2) The one-time bill — capital gains tax (the "transfer tax").** When you sell, you're taxed on the *gain*, not the sale price:
segments.tr: **2) 一次性税单——资本利得税（“转让税”）。** 当你出售时，你是根据*收益*而非销售价格纳税：

segments.src: gain = amount realized (sale price − selling costs) − adjusted basis
segments.tr: gain = amount realized (sale price − selling costs) − adjusted basis

segments.src: adjusted basis = purchase price + capital improvements − depreciation taken
segments.tr: adjusted basis = purchase price + capital improvements − depreciation taken

segments.src: Hold longer than one year and the gain gets **long-term capital gains** rates (0%, 15%, or 20% federally, depending on income), plus a possible 3.8% Net Investment Income Tax at higher incomes, plus state tax.
segments.tr: 持有超过一年，收益将适用**长期资本利得**税率（联邦税率为 0%、15% 或 20%，具体取决于收入），外加高收入人群可能适用的 3.8% 净投资所得税，以及州税。

segments.src: Sell within a year and it's taxed as ordinary income — a materially worse outcome.
segments.tr: 一年内出售则按普通收入纳税——这是一个明显更糟糕的结果。

segments.src: **The wrinkle that surprises everyone: depreciation recapture.** While you own a rental, the IRS lets you deduct the *building* (never the land) over **27.5 years** for residential property or **39 years** for commercial — a paper expense that shelters real cash income.
segments.tr: **让每个人都感到惊讶的棘手问题：折旧回拨 (depreciation recapture)。** 在你拥有出租房期间，国税局 (IRS) 允许你对*建筑物*（绝不是土地）进行折旧扣除，住宅物业为 **27.5 年**，商业物业为 **39 年**——这是一种纸面上的费用，可以抵扣真实的现金收入。

segments.src: But at sale, the depreciation you took gets pulled back into the gain as *unrecaptured Section 1250 gain*, taxed at up to 25%.
segments.tr: 但在出售时，你之前提取的折旧会被收回并计入收益，作为*未回拨的第 1250 条款收益 (unrecaptured Section 1250 gain)*，税率最高可达 25%。

segments.src: Depreciation is a deferral, not a gift.
segments.tr: 折旧是一种延期，而不是礼物。

segments.src: And here's the trap: the IRS computes recapture on depreciation "allowed or allowable" — you owe it whether or not you actually claimed the deduction.
segments.tr: 这里有个陷阱：国税局根据“允许或应允许”的折旧计算回拨——无论你是否实际申报了该扣除，你都欠这笔税。

segments.src: Three legal off-ramps are worth knowing by name:
segments.tr: 有三种合法的避税途径值得了解：

segments.src: - **Section 121 exclusion** — sell your *primary residence* after living in it 2 of the last 5 years and exclude up to **$250,000** of gain (single) or **$500,000** (married filing jointly).
segments.tr: - **第 121 条款排除 (Section 121 exclusion)** — 出售你的*主要住所*，在过去 5 年中居住满 2 年，即可排除最高 **250,000 美元**（单身）或 **500,000 美元**（已婚联合申报）的收益。

segments.src: - **Section 1031 like-kind exchange** — on *investment* property, roll the proceeds into another investment property and defer the gain. Strict clock: identify replacement property within **45 days**, close within **180 days**, and a qualified intermediary must hold the money. Since 2018 this applies to real property only.
segments.tr: - **第 1031 条款同类交换 (Section 1031 like-kind exchange)** — 对于*投资*房产，将收益投入到另一处投资房产中，从而延期缴纳资本利得税。时间限制严格：在 **45 天**内确定置换房产，在 **180 天**内完成交易，并且必须由合格的中介机构持有资金。自 2018 年起，这仅适用于不动产。

segments.src: - **Step-up in basis at death** — heirs generally inherit at fair market value, which can erase decades of embedded gain.
segments.tr: - **死亡时的计税基础调整 (Step-up in basis at death)** — 继承人通常按公平市场价值继承，这可以抹去几十年来积累的收益。

segments.src: Say you buy a single-family rental in Columbus, Ohio for **$300,000**.
segments.tr: 假设你在俄亥俄州哥伦布市购买了一套单户出租房，价格为 **300,000 美元**。

segments.src: The county allocates $60,000 to land and $240,000 to the building.
segments.tr: 县政府将 60,000 美元分配给土地，240,000 美元分配给建筑物。

segments.src: You put $150,000 down and borrow $150,000 at 6.5%.
segments.tr: 你支付了 150,000 美元首付，并以 6.5% 的利率借款 150,000 美元。
你的抵押贷款每月成本约为 948 美元，即每年 11,377 美元。

segments.src: So your actual **cash flow is about $3,546**.
segments.tr: 所以你实际的**现金流约为 3,546 美元**。

segments.src: **Now the tax side of the same year:**
You put roughly $3,500 of cash in your pocket and report a **$3,500 loss**.
segments.tr: 你口袋里装了大约 3,500 美元的现金，但申报了 **3,500 美元的亏损**。

segments.src: That gap is depreciation doing its job.
segments.tr: 这个差距就是折旧在发挥作用。

segments.src: (Whether you can *use* that loss is a separate question — rental losses are generally "passive," though there's a special allowance of up to $25,000 for active participants, which phases out between $100,000 and $150,000 of modified AGI.)
segments.tr: （你是否能“使用”该亏损是另一个问题——出租亏损通常是“被动”的，尽管对于积极参与者有最高 25,000 美元的特殊津贴，该津贴在调整后总收入 (AGI) 100,000 美元至 150,000 美元之间逐步递减。）

segments.src: One nice detail: property taxes on a *rental* are an ordinary business expense on Schedule E and are **not** subject to the SALT cap that limits state and local tax deductions on your personal return.
segments.tr: 一个不错的细节：*出租房*的房产税是 Schedule E 上的普通商业费用，并且**不**受限制个人申报中州和地方税扣除额的 SALT 上限影响。

segments.src: The same dollar of property tax is treated very differently depending on whether you live in the house or rent it out.
segments.tr: 同一美元的房产税，根据你是自住还是出租，处理方式截然不同。

segments.src: **Ten years later, you sell for $400,000** with 6% selling costs:
segments.tr: **十年后，你以 400,000 美元的价格出售**，销售成本为 6%：

segments.src: Notice: the property appreciated $100,000, but your taxable gain is $163,270.
segments.tr: 注意：房产增值了 100,000 美元，但你的应纳税收益是 163,270 美元。

segments.src: The extra $63,000-odd is the bill for ten years of depreciation deductions coming due — which is precisely why 1031 exchanges exist.
segments.tr: 多出的 63,000 多美元是十年折旧扣除额到期应付的账单——这正是 1031 交换存在的原因。

segments.src: 1. Property management protects NOI day to day; asset management decides when to hold, improve, refinance, or sell.
segments.tr: 1. 物业管理保护日常的 NOI；资产管理决定何时持有、改善、再融资或出售。

segments.src: 2. Property tax is local, annual, and permanent — effective rates range from under 0.5% to over 2% of value, so the *location* of a purchase is also a tax decision.
segments.tr: 2. 房产税是地方性的、年度性的且永久的——有效税率从价值的 0.5% 以下到 2% 以上不等，因此购买的*地点*也是一项税务决策。

segments.src: 3. Capital gains tax is computed on gain over adjusted basis, and depreciation lowers that basis — so the deduction you enjoy while holding is largely a deferral you settle at sale.
segments.tr: 3. 资本利得税是根据调整后计税基础之上的收益计算的，而折旧降低了该基础——因此你在持有期间享受的扣除额在很大程度上是一种延期，你在出售时需要结清。

segments.src: **1.** Which of the following is **excluded** from operating expenses when calculating NOI?
segments.tr: **1.** 在计算 NOI 时，以下哪项**不包括**在运营费用中？

segments.src: a) Property taxes   b) Property management fees   c) Mortgage principal and interest   d) Landlord-paid insurance
segments.tr: a) 房产税   b) 物业管理费   c) 抵押贷款本金和利息   d) 房东支付的保险

segments.src: **2.** True or False: Residential rental buildings are depreciated over 27.5 years, and the land is depreciated over the same period.
segments.tr: **2.** 对或错：住宅出租建筑物的折旧年限为 27.5 年，土地的折旧年限相同。

segments.src: **3.** You bought a rental for $300,000, made $20,000 of capital improvements, and took $50,000 of depreciation.
segments.tr: **3.** 你以 300,000 美元购买了一处出租房，进行了 20,000 美元的资本改良，并提取了 50,000 美元的折旧。
你的调整后计税基础是多少？

segments.src: - **NOI (Net Operating Income)** — Effective gross income minus operating expenses, before financing and depreciation; the standard measure of a property's earning power.
segments.tr: - **NOI (净营业收入)** — 有效总收入减去运营费用，在融资和折旧之前；衡量房产盈利能力的标准指标。

segments.src: - **Assessed value / mill rate** — The value a local assessor assigns to a property, and the tax rate applied to it, quoted as dollars per $1,000 of value.
segments.tr: - **评估价值 / 密尔税率 (Assessed value / mill rate)** — 当地评估员分配给房产的价值，以及应用于该价值的税率，以每 1,000 美元价值对应的美元金额报价。

segments.src: - **Adjusted basis** — Purchase price plus capital improvements minus depreciation taken; the number your sale proceeds are measured against to compute gain.
segments.tr: - **调整后计税基础 (Adjusted basis)** — 购买价格加上资本改良减去已提取的折旧；用于衡量销售收益的基准数字。

segments.src: - **Depreciation recapture (unrecaptured §1250 gain)** — The portion of gain attributable to depreciation you previously deducted, taxed at up to 25% at sale.
segments.tr: - **折旧回拨 (未回拨的 §1250 收益)** — 归因于你之前扣除的折旧部分的收益，在出售时最高按 25% 的税率征税。

segments.src: - **Section 1031 exchange** — A swap of one investment property for another that defers capital gains tax, subject to 45-day identification and 180-day closing deadlines.
segments.tr: - **第 1031 条款交换 (Section 1031 exchange)** — 一种将一处投资房产置换为另一处房产的交易，可延期缴纳资本利得税，需遵守 45 天确定期限和 180 天成交期限。

segments.tr: *这是一份关于美国房地产税收结构如何运作的教育性概述，并非税务建议。

segments.src: real estate taxation is structured, not tax advice.
segments.tr: 税率、门槛和上限会随立法而变化，并因州而异——在采取行动前，请与注册会计师 (CPA) 确认当前数据。*

segments.src: Rates, thresholds, and caps change with legislation and vary by state — confirm current figures with a CPA before acting.*

segments.tr: NOI 刻意排除了债务偿还，以便在不考虑融资方式的情况下独立评估房产。

segments.src: NOI deliberately excludes debt service so the property can be compared independently of how it was financed.

segments.tr: 27.5 年的折旧表仅适用于建筑物；土地从不折旧，这就是为什么购买价格必须在两者之间进行分配的原因。

segments.src: The 27.5-year schedule applies to the building only; land is never depreciated, which is why the purchase price must be allocated between the two.

segments.tr: $300,000 + $20,000 − $50,000 = $270,000；你提取的每一美元折旧都会降低你的计税基础，从而增加你最终的应纳税收益。*

segments.src: $300,000 + $20,000 − $50,000 = $270,000; every dollar of depreciation you take lowers your basis and therefore raises your eventual taxable gain.*
segments.tr: $300,000 + $20,000 − $50,000 = $270,000; 您获得的每一美元折旧都会降低您的计税基础，从而增加您最终的应税收益。*

hi.title: [Real Estate 101 #14] आपकी संपत्ति आपको दो टैक्स बिल भेजती है — एक हर साल, एक केवल एक बार

segments.src: > Owning real estate means paying tax while you hold it and tax when you sell it — and good management is largely the work of shrinking both without shrinking the asset.
segments.tr: > अचल संपत्ति (real estate) के स्वामित्व का मतलब है इसे अपने पास रखने के दौरान टैक्स देना और इसे बेचने पर टैक्स देना — और अच्छा प्रबंधन काफी हद तक संपत्ति को कम किए बिना दोनों को कम करने का काम है।

segments.src: Most people think of a property as a thing you buy.
segments.tr: ज्यादातर लोग संपत्ति को एक ऐसी चीज के रूप में सोचते हैं जिसे आप खरीदते हैं।

segments.src: In practice it's a small business you run, and like any business it has an operating side and a tax side.
segments.tr: व्यावहारिक रूप से यह एक छोटा व्यवसाय है जिसे आप चलाते हैं, और किसी भी व्यवसाय की तरह इसका एक परिचालन पक्ष (operating side) और एक कर पक्ष (tax side) होता है।

segments.src: *Property management* is the day-to-day: finding tenants, collecting rent, fixing the water heater at 11 p.m., handling turnovers, keeping the building code-compliant.
segments.tr: *संपत्ति प्रबंधन* दिन-प्रतिदिन का काम है: किरायेदारों को ढूंढना, किराया वसूलना, रात 11 बजे वॉटर हीटर ठीक करना, टर्नओवर संभालना, इमारत को बिल्डिंग कोड के अनुरूप रखना।

segments.src: In the U.S., a residential property manager typically charges **8–10% of collected rent**, often plus a leasing fee of half to one month's rent each time a unit turns over.
segments.tr: अमेरिका में, एक आवासीय संपत्ति प्रबंधक आमतौर पर **वसूले गए किराए का 8–10%** शुल्क लेता है, अक्सर इसके अलावा हर बार यूनिट बदलने पर आधे से एक महीने के किराए का लीजिंग शुल्क भी लिया जाता है।

segments.src: *Asset management* is the level above it: Should we hold or sell?
segments.tr: *परिसंपत्ति प्रबंधन* इसके ऊपर का स्तर है: क्या हमें इसे रखना चाहिए या बेचना चाहिए?

segments.src: Spend $40,000 on a kitchen renovation to push rents, or spend nothing and harvest cash?
segments.tr: किराया बढ़ाने के लिए रसोई के नवीनीकरण पर $40,000 खर्च करें, या कुछ भी खर्च न करें और नकद प्राप्त करें?

segments.src: Property management protects the income; asset management decides what the income is *for*.
segments.tr: संपत्ति प्रबंधन आय की रक्षा करता है; परिसंपत्ति प्रबंधन यह तय करता है कि आय *किस लिए* है।

segments.src: Both are measured through one number: **Net Operating Income (NOI)**.
segments.tr: दोनों को एक संख्या के माध्यम से मापा जाता है: **शुद्ध परिचालन आय (Net Operating Income - NOI)**।

segments.src: NOI = effective gross income − operating expenses
segments.tr: NOI = effective gross income − operating expenses

segments.src: Operating expenses include property taxes, insurance, maintenance, management fees, and utilities you cover.

segments.src: Two things worth knowing: most states offer a **homestead exemption** that reduces the taxable value of your primary residence, and every state has a formal **assessment appeal** process.
segments.tr: दो बातें जानने योग्य हैं: अधिकांश राज्य **होमस्टेड छूट (homestead exemption)** प्रदान करते हैं जो आपके प्राथमिक आवास के कर योग्य मूल्य को कम करती है, और हर राज्य में एक औपचारिक **मूल्यांकन अपील (assessment appeal)** प्रक्रिया होती है।

segments.src: Some states also cap how fast assessed value can rise — California's Proposition 13 limits the increase to 2% per year until the property sells, at which point it's reassessed at market value.
segments.tr: कुछ राज्य यह भी सीमित करते हैं कि निर्धारित मूल्य कितनी तेजी से बढ़ सकता है — कैलिफोर्निया का प्रस्ताव 13 वृद्धि को प्रति वर्ष 2% तक सीमित करता है जब तक कि संपत्ति बिक नहीं जाती, जिस बिंदु पर इसका बाजार मूल्य पर पुनर्मूल्यांकन किया जाता है।

segments.src: **2) The one-time bill — capital gains tax (the "transfer tax").** When you sell, you're taxed on the *gain*, not the sale price:
segments.tr: **2) एकमुश्त बिल — पूंजीगत लाभ कर (capital gains tax) ("हस्तांतरण कर")।** जब आप बेचते हैं, तो आपसे बिक्री मूल्य पर नहीं, बल्कि *लाभ* पर कर लिया जाता है:

segments.src: Hold longer than one year and the gain gets **long-term capital gains** rates (0%, 15%, or 20% federally, depending on income), plus a possible 3.8% Net Investment Income Tax at higher incomes, plus state tax.
segments.tr: एक वर्ष से अधिक समय तक रखें और लाभ पर **दीर्घकालिक पूंजीगत लाभ (long-term capital gains)** दरें लागू होती हैं (आय के आधार पर संघीय रूप से 0%, 15%, या 20%), साथ ही उच्च आय पर संभावित 3.8% शुद्ध निवेश आय कर, और राज्य कर।

segments.src: Sell within a year and it's taxed as ordinary income — a materially worse outcome.
segments.tr: एक वर्ष के भीतर बेचें और इसे सामान्य आय के रूप में कर लगाया जाता है — जो कि काफी खराब परिणाम है।

segments.src: **The wrinkle that surprises everyone: depreciation recapture.** While you own a rental, the IRS lets you deduct the *building* (never the land) over **27.5 years** for residential property or **39 years** for commercial — a paper expense that shelters real cash income.
segments.tr: **वह पेच जो सबको हैरान करता है: मूल्यह्रास पुनरावृत्ति (depreciation recapture)।** जब आप रेंटल के मालिक होते हैं, तो IRS आपको आवासीय संपत्ति के लिए **27.5 वर्षों** या वाणिज्यिक के लिए **39 वर्षों** में *इमारत* (कभी भी जमीन नहीं) को घटाने की अनुमति देता है — एक कागजी खर्च जो वास्तविक नकद आय को सुरक्षित करता है।

segments.src: But at sale, the depreciation you took gets pulled back into the gain as *unrecaptured Section 1250 gain*, taxed at up to 25%.
segments.tr: लेकिन बिक्री के समय, आपके द्वारा लिया गया मूल्यह्रास *अपुनर्प्राप्त धारा 1250 लाभ (unrecaptured Section 1250 gain)* के रूप में लाभ में वापस खींच लिया जाता है, जिस पर बिक्री पर 25% तक कर लगता है।

segments.src: Depreciation is a deferral, not a gift.
segments.tr: मूल्यह्रास एक स्थगन (deferral) है, उपहार नहीं।

segments.src: And here's the trap: the IRS computes recapture on depreciation "allowed or allowable" — you owe it whether or not you actually claimed the deduction.
segments.tr: और यहाँ जाल है: IRS मूल्यह्रास पर पुनरावृत्ति की गणना "अनुमत या स्वीकार्य" के आधार पर करता है — आप इसके लिए उत्तरदायी हैं चाहे आपने वास्तव में कटौती का दावा किया हो या नहीं।

segments.src: Three legal off-ramps are worth knowing by name:
segments.tr: तीन कानूनी रास्ते जानने लायक हैं:

segments.src: - **Section 121 exclusion** — sell your *primary residence* after living in it 2 of the last 5 years and exclude up to **$250,000** of gain (single) or **$500,000** (married filing jointly).
segments.tr: - **धारा 121 बहिष्करण (Section 121 exclusion)** — पिछले 5 वर्षों में से 2 वर्ष अपने *प्राथमिक आवास* में रहने के बाद इसे बेचें और **$250,000** (एकल) या **$500,000** (विवाहित संयुक्त फाइलिंग) तक के लाभ को बाहर रखें।

segments.src: - **Section 1031 like-kind exchange** — on *investment* property, roll the proceeds into another investment property and defer the gain. Strict clock: identify replacement property within **45 days**, close within **180 days**, and a qualified intermediary must hold the money. Since 2018 this applies to real property only.
segments.tr: - **धारा 1031 समान-प्रकार का विनिमय (Section 1031 like-kind exchange)** — *निवेश* संपत्ति पर, आय को दूसरी निवेश संपत्ति में डालें और लाभ को स्थगित करें। सख्त समय सीमा: **45 दिनों** के भीतर प्रतिस्थापन संपत्ति की पहचान करें, **180 दिनों** के भीतर बंद करें, और एक योग्य मध्यस्थ के पास पैसा होना चाहिए। 2018 से यह केवल अचल संपत्ति पर लागू होता है।

segments.src: - **Step-up in basis at death** — heirs generally inherit at fair market value, which can erase decades of embedded gain.
segments.tr: - **मृत्यु पर आधार में वृद्धि (Step-up in basis at death)** — वारिस आमतौर पर उचित बाजार मूल्य पर विरासत में प्राप्त करते हैं, जो दशकों के अंतर्निहित लाभ को मिटा सकता है।

segments.src: - **NOI (Net Operating Income)** — Effective gross income minus operating expenses, before financing and depreciation; the standard measure of a property's earning power.
segments.tr: - **NOI (शुद्ध परिचालन आय)** — प्रभावी सकल आय में से परिचालन खर्च घटाकर, वित्तपोषण और मूल्यह्रास से पहले; संपत्ति की कमाई की शक्ति का मानक माप।

segments.src: - **Assessed value / mill rate** — The value a local assessor assigns to a property, and the tax rate applied to it, quoted as dollars per $1,000 of value.
segments.tr: - **निर्धारित मूल्य / मिल दर (Assessed value / mill rate)** — वह मूल्य जो एक स्थानीय निर्धारक संपत्ति को सौंपता है, और उस पर लागू कर दर, जिसे मूल्य के प्रति $1,000 पर डॉलर के रूप में उद्धृत किया जाता है।

segments.src: - **Adjusted basis** — Purchase price plus capital improvements minus depreciation taken; the number your sale proceeds are measured against to compute gain.
segments.tr: - **समायोजित आधार (Adjusted basis)** — खरीद मूल्य प्लस पूंजीगत सुधार माइनस लिया गया मूल्यह्रास; वह संख्या जिसके मुकाबले लाभ की गणना करने के लिए आपकी बिक्री आय को मापा जाता है।

segments.src: - **Depreciation recapture (unrecaptured §1250 gain)** — The portion of gain attributable to depreciation you previously deducted, taxed at up to 25% at sale.
segments.tr: - **मूल्यह्रास पुनरावृत्ति (अपुनर्प्राप्त §1250 लाभ)** — लाभ का वह हिस्सा जो आपके द्वारा पहले कटौती किए गए मूल्यह्रास के लिए जिम्मेदार है, जिस पर बिक्री पर 25% तक कर लगता है।

segments.src: - **Section 1031 exchange** — A swap of one investment property for another that defers capital gains tax, subject to 45-day identification and 180-day closing deadlines.
segments.tr: - **धारा 1031 विनिमय (Section 1031 exchange)** — एक निवेश संपत्ति का दूसरी के लिए अदला-बदली जो पूंजीगत लाभ कर को स्थगित करती है, 45-दिवसीय पहचान और 180-दिवसीय समापन समय सीमा के अधीन।

es.title: [Bienes Raíces 101 #14] Su propiedad le envía dos facturas de impuestos: una cada año, otra solo una vez

segments.src: > Owning real estate means paying tax while you hold it and tax when you sell it — and good management is largely the work of shrinking both without shrinking the asset.
segments.tr: > Poseer bienes raíces significa pagar impuestos mientras los conserva e impuestos cuando los vende; y una buena gestión consiste en gran medida en reducir ambos sin reducir el activo.

segments.src: Most people think of a property as a thing you buy.
segments.tr: La mayoría de la gente piensa en una propiedad como algo que se compra.

segments.src: In practice it's a small business you run, and like any business it has an operating side and a tax side.
segments.tr: En la práctica, es un pequeño negocio que usted dirige y, como cualquier negocio, tiene un lado operativo y un lado fiscal.
**El lado operativo: gestión de propiedades frente a

segments.src: *Property management* is the day-to-day: finding tenants, collecting rent, fixing the water heater at 11 p.m., handling turnovers, keeping the building code-compliant.
segments.tr: La *gestión de propiedades* es el día a día: encontrar inquilinos, cobrar el alquiler, arreglar el calentador de agua a las 11 p. m., gestionar los cambios de inquilino y mantener el edificio cumpliendo con los códigos.

segments.src: In the U.S., a residential property manager typically charges **8–10% of collected rent**, often plus a leasing fee of half to one month's rent each time a unit turns over.
segments.tr: En EE. UU., un administrador de propiedades residenciales suele cobrar **entre el 8 y el 10 % del alquiler cobrado**, a menudo más una tarifa de arrendamiento de medio a un mes de alquiler cada vez que una unidad cambia de inquilino.

segments.src: *Asset management* is the level above it: Should we hold or sell?
segments.tr: La *gestión de activos* es el nivel superior: ¿Debemos conservar o vender?

segments.src: Spend $40,000 on a kitchen renovation to push rents, or spend nothing and harvest cash?
segments.tr: ¿Gastar $40,000 en una renovación de cocina para subir los alquileres, o no gastar nada y obtener efectivo?

segments.src: Property management protects the income; asset management decides what the income is *for*.
segments.tr: La gestión de propiedades protege los ingresos; la gestión de activos decide para *qué* son esos ingresos.

segments.src: Both are measured through one number: **Net Operating Income (NOI)**.
segments.tr: Ambos se miden a través de un número: **Ingreso Operativo Neto (NOI)**.

segments.src: NOI = effective gross income − operating expenses
segments.tr: NOI = effective gross income − operating expenses

segments.src: Operating expenses include property taxes, insurance, maintenance, management fees, and utilities you cover.
segments.tr: Los gastos operativos incluyen impuestos a la propiedad, seguros, mantenimiento, tarifas de administración y servicios públicos que usted cubre.

segments.src: They **exclude** your mortgage payment and depreciation.
segments.tr: **Excluyen** el pago de su hipoteca y la depreciación.

segments.src: That's deliberate — NOI describes the property, not your financing.
segments.tr: Eso es deliberado: el NOI describe la propiedad, no su financiamiento.

segments.src: **The tax side: two very different bills.**
segments.tr: **El lado fiscal: dos facturas muy diferentes.**

segments.src: **1) The annual bill — property tax (the "holding tax").** In the U.S.
segments.tr: **1) La factura anual: impuesto a la propiedad (el "impuesto de retención").** En EE. UU.

segments.src: this is levied locally, not federally: by counties, cities, and school districts.
segments.tr: esto se cobra a nivel local, no federal: por condados, ciudades y distritos escolares.

segments.src: The county assessor sets an *assessed value*, and a tax rate (often quoted in *mills* — dollars per $1,000 of value) is applied to it.
segments.tr: El tasador del condado establece un *valor tasado* y se le aplica una tasa impositiva (a menudo cotizada en *mills* — dólares por cada $1,000 de valor).

segments.src: Effective rates vary enormously — roughly 0.3% of market value in Hawaii to well over 2% in New Jersey and parts of Illinois and Texas.
segments.tr: Las tasas efectivas varían enormemente: desde aproximadamente el 0.3 % del valor de mercado en Hawái hasta más del 2 % en Nueva Jersey y partes de Illinois y Texas.

segments.src: On the same $400,000 house, that's the difference between about $1,200 and $8,800 a year, every year, forever.
segments.tr: En la misma casa de $400,000, esa es la diferencia entre unos $1,200 y $8,800 al año, todos los años, para siempre.

segments.src: Two things worth knowing: most states offer a **homestead exemption** that reduces the taxable value of your primary residence, and every state has a formal **assessment appeal** process.
segments.tr: Dos cosas que vale la pena saber: la mayoría de los estados ofrecen una **exención de vivienda principal** (homestead exemption) que reduce el valor gravable de su residencia principal, y cada estado tiene un proceso formal de **apelación de tasación**.

segments.src: Some states also cap how fast assessed value can rise — California's Proposition 13 limits the increase to 2% per year until the property sells, at which point it's reassessed at market value.
segments.tr: Algunos estados también limitan la velocidad a la que puede subir el valor tasado; la Propuesta 13 de California limita el aumento al 2 % anual hasta que se vende la propiedad, momento en el cual se vuelve a tasar al valor de mercado.

segments.src: **2) The one-time bill — capital gains tax (the "transfer tax").** When you sell, you're taxed on the *gain*, not the sale price:
segments.tr: **2) La factura única: impuesto sobre las ganancias de capital (el "impuesto de transferencia").** Cuando vende, se le grava sobre la *ganancia*, no sobre el precio de venta:

segments.src: gain = amount realized (sale price − selling costs) − adjusted basis
segments.tr: gain = amount realized (sale price − selling costs) − adjusted basis

segments.src: adjusted basis = purchase price + capital improvements − depreciation taken
segments.tr: adjusted basis = purchase price + capital improvements − depreciation taken

segments.src: Hold longer than one year and the gain gets **long-term capital gains** rates (0%, 15%, or 20% federally, depending on income), plus a possible 3.8% Net Investment Income Tax at higher incomes, plus state tax.
segments.tr: Si conserva la propiedad por más de un año, la ganancia recibe las tasas de **ganancias de capital a largo plazo** (0 %, 15 % o 20 % a nivel federal, según los ingresos), más un posible Impuesto sobre la Renta de Inversión Neta del 3.8 % para ingresos más altos, más el impuesto estatal.

segments.src: Sell within a year and it's taxed as ordinary income — a materially worse outcome.
segments.tr: Si vende dentro del año, se grava como ingreso ordinario, un resultado materialmente peor.

segments.src: **The wrinkle that surprises everyone: depreciation recapture.** While you own a rental, the IRS lets you deduct the *building* (never the land) over **27.5 years** for residential property or **39 years** for commercial — a paper expense that shelters real cash income.
segments.tr: **El detalle que sorprende a todos: la recuperación de la depreciación.** Mientras posee un alquiler, el IRS le permite deducir el *edificio* (nunca el terreno) durante **27.5 años** para propiedades residenciales o **39 años** para comerciales; un gasto en papel que protege los ingresos en efectivo reales.

segments.src: But at sale, the depreciation you took gets pulled back into the gain as *unrecaptured Section 1250 gain*, taxed at up to 25%.
segments.tr: Pero al momento de la venta, la depreciación que tomó se vuelve a incluir en la ganancia como *ganancia no recuperada de la Sección 1250*, gravada hasta en un 25 %.

segments.src: Depreciation is a deferral, not a gift.
segments.tr: La depreciación es un aplazamiento, no un regalo.

segments.src: And here's the trap: the IRS computes recapture on depreciation "allowed or allowable" — you owe it whether or not you actually claimed the deduction.
segments.tr: Y aquí está la trampa: el IRS calcula la recuperación sobre la depreciación "permitida o permisible"; usted la debe, haya reclamado o no la deducción.

segments.src: Three legal off-ramps are worth knowing by name:
segments.tr: Tres salidas legales que vale la pena conocer por su nombre:

segments.src: - **Section 121 exclusion** — sell your *primary residence* after living in it 2 of the last 5 years and exclude up to **$250,000** of gain (single) or **$500,000** (married filing jointly).
segments.tr: - **Exclusión de la Sección 121** — venda su *residencia principal* después de vivir en ella 2 de los últimos 5 años y excluya hasta **$250,000** de ganancia (soltero) o **$500,000** (casados que presentan declaración conjunta).

segments.src: - **Section 1031 like-kind exchange** — on *investment* property, roll the proceeds into another investment property and defer the gain. Strict clock: identify replacement property within **45 days**, close within **180 days**, and a qualified intermediary must hold the money. Since 2018 this applies to real property only.
segments.tr: - **Intercambio de tipo similar de la Sección 1031** — en propiedad de *inversión*, transfiera las ganancias a otra propiedad de inversión y posponga la ganancia. Plazo estricto: identifique la propiedad de reemplazo dentro de los **45 días**, cierre dentro de los **180 días** y un intermediario calificado debe retener el dinero. Desde 2018, esto se aplica únicamente a bienes raíces.

segments.src: - **Step-up in basis at death** — heirs generally inherit at fair market value, which can erase decades of embedded gain.
segments.tr: - **Aumento de la base por fallecimiento (Step-up in basis)** — los herederos generalmente heredan al valor justo de mercado, lo que puede borrar décadas de ganancias incorporadas.

segments.src: Say you buy a single-family rental in Columbus, Ohio for **$300,000**.
segments.tr: Suponga que compra una propiedad de alquiler unifamiliar en Columbus, Ohio, por **$300,000**.

segments.src: The county allocates $60,000 to land and $240,000 to the building.
segments.tr: El condado asigna $60,000 al terreno y $240,000 al edificio.

segments.tr: Usted aporta $150,000 de inicial y pide prestados $150,000 al 6.5%.
Los costos de su hipoteca son de aproximadamente $948 al mes, o $11,377 al año.

segments.src: So your actual **cash flow is about $3,546**.
segments.tr: Así que su **flujo de efectivo real es de aproximadamente $3,546**.

segments.src: **Now the tax side of the same year:**
segments.tr: **Ahora el lado fiscal del mismo año:**

segments.src: You put roughly $3,500 of cash in your pocket and report a **$3,500 loss**.
segments.tr: Usted se pone aproximadamente $3,500 en efectivo en el bolsillo y reporta una **pérdida de $3,500**.

segments.src: That gap is depreciation doing its job.
segments.tr: Esa brecha es la depreciación haciendo su trabajo.

segments.src: (Whether you can *use* that loss is a separate question — rental losses are generally "passive," though there's a special allowance of up to $25,000 for active participants, which phases out between $100,000 and $150,000 of modified AGI.)
segments.tr: (Si puede *usar* esa pérdida es una pregunta separada; las pérdidas por alquiler son generalmente "pasivas", aunque hay una asignación especial de hasta $25,000 para participantes activos, que se elimina gradualmente entre $100,000 y $150,000 de AGI modificado).

segments.src: One nice detail: property taxes on a *rental* are an ordinary business expense on Schedule E and are **not** subject to the SALT cap that limits state and local tax deductions on your personal return.
segments.tr: Un detalle agradable: los impuestos a la propiedad de un *alquiler* son un gasto comercial ordinario en el Anexo E (Schedule E) y **no** están sujetos al límite SALT que limita las deducciones de impuestos estatales y locales en su declaración personal.

segments.src: The same dollar of property tax is treated very differently depending on whether you live in the house or rent it out.
segments.tr: El mismo dólar de impuesto a la propiedad se trata de manera muy diferente según si vive en la casa o la alquila.

segments.src: **Ten years later, you sell for $400,000** with 6% selling costs:
segments.tr: **Diez años después, vende por $400,000** con costos de venta del 6%:

segments.src: Notice: the property appreciated $100,000, but your taxable gain is $163,270.
segments.tr: Aviso: la propiedad se aprecio $100,000, pero su ganancia gravable es de $163,270.

segments.src: The extra $63,000-odd is the bill for ten years of depreciation deductions coming due — which is precisely why 1031 exchanges exist.
segments.tr: Los $63,000 adicionales más o menos son la factura de diez años de deducciones por depreciación que llegan a su vencimiento, lo cual es precisamente la razón por la cual existen los intercambios 1031.

segments.src: 1. Property management protects NOI day to day; asset management decides when to hold, improve, refinance, or sell.
segments.tr: 1. La gestión de propiedades protege el NOI día a día; la gestión de activos decide cuándo retener, mejorar, refinanciar o vender.

segments.src: 2. Property tax is local, annual, and permanent — effective rates range from under 0.5% to over 2% of value, so the *location* of a purchase is also a tax decision.
segments.tr: 2. El impuesto a la propiedad es local, anual y permanente; las tasas efectivas oscilan entre menos del 0.5% y más del 2% del valor, por lo que la *ubicación* de una compra también es una decisión fiscal.

segments.src: 3. Capital gains tax is computed on gain over adjusted basis, and depreciation lowers that basis — so the deduction you enjoy while holding is largely a deferral you settle at sale.
segments.tr: 3. El impuesto sobre las ganancias de capital se calcula sobre la ganancia por encima de la base ajustada, y la depreciación reduce esa base; por lo tanto, la deducción de la que disfruta mientras posee la propiedad es en gran medida un aplazamiento que liquida al vender.

segments.src: - **NOI (Net Operating Income)** — Effective gross income minus operating expenses, before financing and depreciation; the standard measure of a property's earning power.
segments.tr: - **NOI (Ingreso Operativo Neto)** — Ingreso bruto efectivo menos gastos operativos, antes de financiamiento y depreciación; la medida estándar del poder de ganancia de una propiedad.

segments.src: - **Assessed value / mill rate** — The value a local assessor assigns to a property, and the tax rate applied to it, quoted as dollars per $1,000 of value.
segments.tr: - **Valor tasado / tasa de millaje (Assessed value / mill rate)** — El valor que un tasador local asigna a una propiedad y la tasa impositiva aplicada a ella, cotizada como dólares por cada $1,000 de valor.

segments.src: - **Adjusted basis** — Purchase price plus capital improvements minus depreciation taken; the number your sale proceeds are measured against to compute gain.
segments.tr: - **Base ajustada (Adjusted basis)** — Precio de compra más mejoras de capital menos la depreciación tomada; el número con el que se comparan los ingresos de su venta para calcular la ganancia.

segments.src: - **Depreciation recapture (unrecaptured §1250 gain)** — The portion of gain attributable to depreciation you previously deducted, taxed at up to 25% at sale.
segments.tr: - **Recuperación de la depreciación (ganancia no recuperada de la §1250)** — La porción de la ganancia atribuible a la depreciación que dedujo anteriormente, gravada hasta en un 25% al vender.

segments.src: - **Section 1031 exchange** — A swap of one investment property for another that defers capital gains tax, subject to 45-day identification and 180-day closing deadlines.
segments.tr: - **Intercambio de la Sección 1031** — Un intercambio de una propiedad de inversión por otra que pospone el impuesto sobre las ganancias de capital, sujeto a plazos de identificación de 45 días y cierre de 180 días.

segments.tr: هناك شيئان يستحقان المعرفة: تقدم معظم الولايات **إعفاءً للمسكن الرئيسي** يقلل من القيمة الخاضعة للضريبة لمسكنك الأساسي، ولكل ولاية عملية رسمية لـ **الطعن في التقييم**.

segments.src: Some states also cap how fast assessed value can rise — California's Proposition 13 limits the increase to 2% per year until the property sells, at which point it's reassessed at market value.
segments.tr: تضع بعض الولايات أيضاً حداً أقصى لسرعة ارتفاع القيمة المقدرة — يحد الاقتراح 13 في كاليفورنيا من الزيادة إلى 2% سنوياً حتى يتم بيع العقار، وعندها يتم إعادة تقييمه بالقيمة السوقية.

segments.src: **2) The one-time bill — capital gains tax (the "transfer tax").** When you sell, you're taxed on the *gain*, not the sale price:
segments.tr: **2) الفاتورة لمرة واحدة — ضريبة الأرباح الرأسمالية ("ضريبة النقل").** عند البيع، تُفرض عليك ضريبة على *الربح*، وليس على سعر البيع:

segments.src: adjusted basis = purchase price + capital improvements − depreciation taken

segments.src: Hold longer than one year and the gain gets **long-term capital gains** rates (0%, 15%, or 20% federally, depending on income), plus a possible 3.8% Net Investment Income Tax at higher incomes, plus state tax.
segments.tr: إذا احتفظت بالعقار لأكثر من عام، يخضع الربح لمعدلات **الأرباح الرأسمالية طويلة الأجل** (0%، 15%، أو 20% فيدرالياً، اعتماداً على الدخل)، بالإضافة إلى ضريبة دخل الاستثمار الصافي المحتملة بنسبة 3.8% عند الدخول الأعلى، بالإضافة إلى ضريبة الولاية.

segments.src: Sell within a year and it's taxed as ordinary income — a materially worse outcome.
segments.tr: إذا بعت في غضون عام، تُفرض الضريبة كدخل عادي — وهي نتيجة أسوأ بكثير.

segments.src: **The wrinkle that surprises everyone: depreciation recapture.** While you own a rental, the IRS lets you deduct the *building* (never the land) over **27.5 years** for residential property or **39 years** for commercial — a paper expense that shelters real cash income.
segments.tr: **التفصيل الذي يفاجئ الجميع: استرداد استهلاك الأصول (Depreciation Recapture).** أثناء امتلاكك لعقار مؤجر، تسمح لك مصلحة الضرائب بخصم تكلفة *المبنى* (وليس الأرض أبداً) على مدى **27.5 عاماً** للعقارات السكنية أو **39 عاماً** للعقارات التجارية — وهي مصروفات ورقية تحمي الدخل النقدي الحقيقي.

segments.src: But at sale, the depreciation you took gets pulled back into the gain as *unrecaptured Section 1250 gain*, taxed at up to 25%.
segments.tr: ولكن عند البيع، يتم سحب الاستهلاك الذي أخذته وإضافته مرة أخرى إلى الربح كـ *ربح غير مسترد بموجب القسم 1250*، ويخضع لضريبة تصل إلى 25%.

segments.src: Depreciation is a deferral, not a gift.
And here's the trap: the IRS computes recapture on depreciation "allowed or allowable" — you owe it whether or not you actually claimed the deduction.
segments.tr: وهنا تكمن الخدعة: تحسب مصلحة الضرائب الاسترداد على الاستهلاك "المسموح به أو القابل للخصم" — أنت مدين به سواء طالبت بالخصم فعلياً أم لا.

segments.src: Three legal off-ramps are worth knowing by name:
segments.tr: هناك ثلاثة مخارج قانونية تستحق المعرفة بالاسم:

segments.src: - **Section 121 exclusion** — sell your *primary residence* after living in it 2 of the last 5 years and exclude up to **$250,000** of gain (single) or **$500,000** (married filing jointly).
segments.tr: - **استثناء القسم 121** — بع *مسكنك الرئيسي* بعد العيش فيه لمدة عامين من أصل آخر 5 سنوات واستثنِ ما يصل إلى **250,000 دولار** من الربح (للأعزب) أو **500,000 دولار** (للمتزوجين الذين يقدمون إقراراً مشتركاً).

segments.src: - **Section 1031 like-kind exchange** — on *investment* property, roll the proceeds into another investment property and defer the gain. Strict clock: identify replacement property within **45 days**, close within **180 days**, and a qualified intermediary must hold the money. Since 2018 this applies to real property only.
segments.tr: - **تبادل القسم 1031 (المماثل)** — بالنسبة للعقارات *الاستثمارية*، قم بتحويل العائدات إلى عقار استثماري آخر وقم بتأجيل الربح. توقيت صارم: حدد العقار البديل في غضون **45 يوماً**، وأغلق الصفقة في غضون **180 يوماً**، ويجب أن يحتفظ وسيط مؤهل بالأموال. منذ عام 2018، ينطبق هذا على العقارات فقط.

segments.src: - **Step-up in basis at death** — heirs generally inherit at fair market value, which can erase decades of embedded gain.
segments.tr: - **رفع الأساس عند الوفاة** — يرث الورثة عادةً بالقيمة السوقية العادلة، مما قد يمحو عقوداً من الأرباح المضمنة.

segments.tr: لنفترض أنك اشتريت عقاراً سكنياً لعائلة واحدة في كولومبوس، أوهايو مقابل **300,000 دولار**.

segments.src: One nice detail: property taxes on a *rental* are an ordinary business expense on Schedule E and are **not** subject to the SALT cap that limits state and local tax deductions on your personal return.
segments.tr: تفصيل لطيف واحد: الضرائب العقارية على *عقار مؤجر* هي مصروفات تجارية عادية في الجدول E و **لا** تخضع لسقف SALT الذي يحد من خصومات الضرائب الحكومية والمحلية في إقرارك الشخصي.

segments.src: - **NOI (Net Operating Income)** — Effective gross income minus operating expenses, before financing and depreciation; the standard measure of a property's earning power.
segments.tr: - **NOI (صافي الدخل التشغيلي)** — إجمالي الدخل الفعلي ناقص المصاريف التشغيلية، قبل التمويل والاستهلاك؛ المقياس القياسي للقوة الربحية للعقار.

segments.src: - **Assessed value / mill rate** — The value a local assessor assigns to a property, and the tax rate applied to it, quoted as dollars per $1,000 of value.
segments.tr: - **القيمة المقدرة / معدل الميل** — القيمة التي يخصصها المقيم المحلي للعقار، والمعدل الضريبي المطبق عليها، ويُشار إليه كدولارات لكل 1,000 دولار من القيمة.

segments.src: - **Adjusted basis** — Purchase price plus capital improvements minus depreciation taken; the number your sale proceeds are measured against to compute gain.
segments.tr: - **الأساس المعدل** — سعر الشراء زائد التحسينات الرأسمالية ناقص الاستهلاك المأخوذ؛ الرقم الذي يتم قياس عائدات البيع الخاصة بك مقابله لحساب الربح.

segments.src: - **Depreciation recapture (unrecaptured §1250 gain)** — The portion of gain attributable to depreciation you previously deducted, taxed at up to 25% at sale.
segments.tr: - **استرداد الاستهلاك (ربح غير مسترد بموجب القسم 1250)** — جزء الربح المنسوب إلى الاستهلاك الذي خصمته سابقاً، ويخضع لضريبة تصل إلى 25% عند البيع.

segments.src: - **Section 1031 exchange** — A swap of one investment property for another that defers capital gains tax, subject to 45-day identification and 180-day closing deadlines.
segments.tr: - **تبادل القسم 1031** — مقايضة عقار استثماري بآخر مما يؤجل ضريبة الأرباح الرأسمالية، ويخضع لمواعيد نهائية للتحديد خلال 45 يوماً والإغلاق خلال 180 يوماً.

fr.title: [Real Estate 101 #14] Votre propriété vous envoie deux factures fiscales — l'une chaque année, l'autre une seule fois

segments.src: > Owning real estate means paying tax while you hold it and tax when you sell it — and good management is largely the work of shrinking both without shrinking the asset.
segments.tr: > Posséder de l'immobilier signifie payer des impôts pendant que vous le détenez et des impôts lorsque vous le vendez — et une bonne gestion consiste en grande partie à réduire les deux sans réduire l'actif.

segments.src: Most people think of a property as a thing you buy.
segments.tr: La plupart des gens voient un bien immobilier comme un objet qu'on achète.

segments.src: In practice it's a small business you run, and like any business it has an operating side and a tax side.
segments.tr: En pratique, c'est une petite entreprise que vous gérez, et comme toute entreprise, elle a un côté opérationnel et un côté fiscal.

segments.src: *Property management* is the day-to-day: finding tenants, collecting rent, fixing the water heater at 11 p.m., handling turnovers, keeping the building code-compliant.
segments.tr: *La gestion immobilière* est le quotidien : trouver des locataires, percevoir les loyers, réparer le chauffe-eau à 23h, gérer les rotations, maintenir le bâtiment conforme aux normes.

segments.src: In the U.S., a residential property manager typically charges **8–10% of collected rent**, often plus a leasing fee of half to one month's rent each time a unit turns over.
segments.tr: Aux États-Unis, un gestionnaire immobilier résidentiel facture généralement **8–10 % du loyer perçu**, souvent en plus de frais de location équivalant à la moitié ou à un mois de loyer à chaque changement de locataire.

segments.src: *Asset management* is the level above it: Should we hold or sell?
segments.tr: *La gestion d'actifs* est le niveau supérieur : devons-nous conserver ou vendre ?

segments.src: Spend $40,000 on a kitchen renovation to push rents, or spend nothing and harvest cash?
segments.tr: Dépenser 40 000 $ pour rénover une cuisine afin d'augmenter les loyers, ou ne rien dépenser et encaisser le cash ?

segments.src: Property management protects the income; asset management decides what the income is *for*.
segments.tr: La gestion immobilière protège les revenus ; la gestion d'actifs décide à quoi servent ces revenus.

segments.src: Both are measured through one number: **Net Operating Income (NOI)**.
segments.tr: Les deux sont mesurés par un seul chiffre : le **bénéfice net d'exploitation (NOI)**.

segments.src: NOI = effective gross income − operating expenses
segments.tr: NOI = effective gross income − operating expenses

segments.src: Operating expenses include property taxes, insurance, maintenance, management fees, and utilities you cover.
segments.tr: Les dépenses d'exploitation comprennent les impôts fonciers, l'assurance, l'entretien, les frais de gestion et les services publics que vous prenez en charge.

segments.src: They **exclude** your mortgage payment and depreciation.
segments.tr: Elles **excluent** votre paiement hypothécaire et l'amortissement.

segments.src: That's deliberate — NOI describes the property, not your financing.
segments.tr: C'est délibéré — le NOI décrit la propriété, pas votre financement.

segments.src: **The tax side: two very different bills.**
segments.tr: **Le côté fiscal : deux factures très différentes.**

segments.src: **1) The annual bill — property tax (the "holding tax").** In the U.S.
segments.tr: **1) La facture annuelle — l'impôt foncier (l'« impôt de détention »).** Aux États-Unis,

segments.src: this is levied locally, not federally: by counties, cities, and school districts.
segments.tr: celui-ci est perçu au niveau local, et non fédéral : par les comtés, les villes et les districts scolaires.

segments.src: The county assessor sets an *assessed value*, and a tax rate (often quoted in *mills* — dollars per $1,000 of value) is applied to it.
segments.tr: L'évaluateur du comté fixe une *valeur évaluée*, et un taux d'imposition (souvent exprimé en *mills* — des dollars par tranche de 1 000 $ de valeur) lui est appliqué.

segments.src: Effective rates vary enormously — roughly 0.3% of market value in Hawaii to well over 2% in New Jersey and parts of Illinois and Texas.
segments.tr: Les taux effectifs varient énormément — d'environ 0,3 % de la valeur marchande à Hawaï à plus de 2 % dans le New Jersey et dans certaines parts de l'Illinois et du Texas.

segments.src: On the same $400,000 house, that's the difference between about $1,200 and $8,800 a year, every year, forever.
segments.tr: Pour une même maison de 400 000 $, c'est la différence entre environ 1 200 $ et 8 800 $ par an, chaque année, pour toujours.

segments.src: Two things worth knowing: most states offer a **homestead exemption** that reduces the taxable value of your primary residence, and every state has a formal **assessment appeal** process.
segments.tr: Deux choses bonnes à savoir : la plupart des États offrent une **exonération de résidence principale** qui réduit la valeur imposable de votre résidence principale, et chaque État dispose d'une procédure formelle d'**appel d'évaluation**.

segments.src: Some states also cap how fast assessed value can rise — California's Proposition 13 limits the increase to 2% per year until the property sells, at which point it's reassessed at market value.
segments.tr: Certains États limitent également la vitesse à laquelle la valeur évaluée peut augmenter — la Proposition 13 de la Californie limite l'augmentation à 2 % par an jusqu'à ce que la propriété soit vendue, moment auquel elle est réévaluée à la valeur marchande.

segments.src: **2) The one-time bill — capital gains tax (the "transfer tax").** When you sell, you're taxed on the *gain*, not the sale price:
segments.tr: **2) La facture unique — l'impôt sur les gains en capital (l'« impôt sur les transferts »).** Lorsque vous vendez, vous êtes imposé sur le *gain*, et non sur le prix de vente :

segments.src: Hold longer than one year and the gain gets **long-term capital gains** rates (0%, 15%, or 20% federally, depending on income), plus a possible 3.8% Net Investment Income Tax at higher incomes, plus state tax.
segments.tr: Détenez le bien plus d'un an et le gain bénéficie des taux des **gains en capital à long terme** (0 %, 15 % ou 20 % au niveau fédéral, selon le revenu), plus un impôt potentiel de 3,8 % sur le revenu net d'investissement pour les revenus plus élevés, plus l'impôt de l'État.

segments.tr: **La subtilité qui surprend tout le monde : la récupération de l'amortissement.** Pendant que vous possédez un bien locatif, l'IRS vous permet de déduire le *bâtiment* (jamais le terrain) sur **27,5 ans** pour un bien résidentiel ou **39 ans** pour un bien commercial — une dépense comptable qui protège les revenus de trésorerie réels.

pt.title: [Real Estate 101 #14] Sua propriedade envia duas contas de imposto — Uma todo ano, uma apenas uma vez

segments.src: > Owning real estate means paying tax while you hold it and tax when you sell it — and good management is largely the work of shrinking both without shrinking the asset.
segments.tr: > Possuir imóveis significa pagar impostos enquanto você os mantém e impostos quando os vende — e uma boa gestão é, em grande parte, o trabalho de reduzir ambos sem diminuir o ativo.

segments.src: Most people think of a property as a thing you buy.
segments.tr: A maioria das pessoas pensa em uma propriedade como algo que você compra.

segments.src: In practice it's a small business you run, and like any business it has an operating side and a tax side.
segments.tr: Na prática, é um pequeno negócio que você administra e, como qualquer negócio, tem um lado operacional e um lado fiscal.
**O lado operacional: gestão de propriedades vs.

segments.src: *Property management* is the day-to-day: finding tenants, collecting rent, fixing the water heater at 11 p.m., handling turnovers, keeping the building code-compliant.
segments.tr: *Gestão de propriedades* é o dia a dia: encontrar inquilinos, cobrar aluguel, consertar o aquecedor de água às 23h, lidar com rotatividades, manter o edifício em conformidade com o código.

segments.src: In the U.S., a residential property manager typically charges **8–10% of collected rent**, often plus a leasing fee of half to one month's rent each time a unit turns over.
segments.tr: Nos EUA, um gerente de propriedade residencial normalmente cobra **8–10% do aluguel coletado**, muitas vezes mais uma taxa de locação de meio a um mês de aluguel cada vez que uma unidade é trocada.

segments.src: *Asset management* is the level above it: Should we hold or sell?
segments.tr: *Gestão de ativos* é o nível acima disso: devemos manter ou vender?

segments.src: Spend $40,000 on a kitchen renovation to push rents, or spend nothing and harvest cash?
segments.tr: Gastar $40.000 em uma reforma de cozinha para aumentar os aluguéis, ou não gastar nada e colher dinheiro?

segments.src: Property management protects the income; asset management decides what the income is *for*.
segments.tr: A gestão de propriedades protege a renda; a gestão de ativos decide para *que* serve a renda.

segments.src: Both are measured through one number: **Net Operating Income (NOI)**.
segments.tr: Ambos são medidos por meio de um número: **Receita Operacional Líquida (NOI)**.

segments.src: NOI = effective gross income − operating expenses
segments.tr: NOI = effective gross income − operating expenses

segments.src: Operating expenses include property taxes, insurance, maintenance, management fees, and utilities you cover.
segments.tr: As despesas operacionais incluem impostos sobre a propriedade, seguro, manutenção, taxas de gestão e serviços públicos que você cobre.

segments.src: They **exclude** your mortgage payment and depreciation.
segments.tr: Elas **excluem** o pagamento da hipoteca e a depreciação.

segments.src: That's deliberate — NOI describes the property, not your financing.
segments.tr: Isso é intencional — o NOI descreve a propriedade, não o seu financiamento.

segments.src: **The tax side: two very different bills.**
segments.tr: **O lado fiscal: duas contas muito diferentes.**

segments.src: **1) The annual bill — property tax (the "holding tax").** In the U.S.
segments.tr: **1) A conta anual — imposto sobre a propriedade (o "imposto de retenção").** Nos EUA,

segments.src: The county assessor sets an *assessed value*, and a tax rate (often quoted in *mills* — dollars per $1,000 of value) is applied to it.
segments.tr: O avaliador do condado define um *valor avaliado*, e uma taxa de imposto (geralmente cotada em *mills* — dólares por $1.000 de valor) é aplicada a ele.

segments.src: Effective rates vary enormously — roughly 0.3% of market value in Hawaii to well over 2% in New Jersey and parts of Illinois and Texas.

segments.tr: Na mesma casa de $400.000, essa é a diferença entre cerca de $1.200 e $8.800 por ano, todos os anos, para sempre.

segments.src: Two things worth knowing: most states offer a **homestead exemption** that reduces the taxable value of your primary residence, and every state has a formal **assessment appeal** process.
segments.tr: Duas coisas que vale a pena saber: a maioria dos estados oferece uma **isenção de residência** que reduz o valor tributável de sua residência principal, e todo estado tem um processo formal de **apelação de avaliação**.

segments.src: Some states also cap how fast assessed value can rise — California's Proposition 13 limits the increase to 2% per year until the property sells, at which point it's reassessed at market value.

segments.src: **The wrinkle that surprises everyone: depreciation recapture.** While you own a rental, the IRS lets you deduct the *building* (never the land) over **27.5 years** for residential property or **39 years** for commercial — a paper expense that shelters real cash income.

segments.src: Depreciation is a deferral, not a gift.
